# pbwire

> pbwire is a dynamic Protobuf runtime for C. It loads a schema at runtime — a hand-built descriptor
> tree or a standard `FileDescriptorSet` — then builds, reads, encodes and decodes messages through
> reflection, speaking the standard Protobuf binary wire format. No code generation, no `protoc` at
> runtime, no libprotobuf in the process: C99, one public header, about 3.4k lines of C, zero runtime
> dependencies.

Facts: source at <https://github.com/jinganix/pbwire>, license Apache-2.0, version `0.1.0`
(`project(pbwire VERSION ...)` in `CMakeLists.txt`). Encodings are byte-identical to `protoc 36.2`
and pass Google's official binary conformance suite: 1391 successes, 0 unexpected failures, 1403
JSON/text tests skipped because pbwire has no JSON layer. Requirements: a C99 compiler for the core;
CMake + C++17 + libprotobuf only for the optional `.proto` importer `pbwire-protoc`.

## Build and test

```bash
make              # build/libpbwire.a
make test         # core + threads + descriptor-set self-checks (required before commit)
make format       # clang-format >= 19; make format-check for the gate

cmake -B build-cmake && cmake --build build-cmake && (cd build-cmake && ctest)
cmake -B build-cmake -DPBW_BUILD_PROTOC=ON   # adds the .proto importer (needs libprotobuf)
```

Optional, needs `protoc` + libprotobuf C++: `make difftest` (differential test against the official
C++ runtime), `make bench`. Optional, needs a protobuf v36.2 source checkout:
`PBWIRE_PROTOBUF_SRC=$PWD/protobuf make conformance`.

## API

- `pbw_schema *pbw_schema_new(void)` / `pbw_schema_free(pbw_schema *)`
- `pbw_descriptor *pbw_schema_add_message(pbw_schema *, const char *name)`, `pbw_schema_add_enum`,
  `pbw_schema_find(const pbw_schema *, const char *name)`; `pbw_schema_link()` resolves type names.
- `pbw_field *pbw_message_add_field(pbw_descriptor *msg, const char *name, uint32_t number,
  pbw_type type, pbw_label label)`; `pbw_field_set_type_name`, `pbw_field_set_packed`,
  `pbw_field_set_oneof`.
- `pbw_status pbw_descriptor_set_load(const void *data, size_t len, pbw_schema **out)`: standard
  `FileDescriptorSet` -> linked schema; `pbw_schema_error()` explains a failure.
- `pbw_message *pbw_message_new(const pbw_descriptor *)`, `pbw_message_free`;
  `pbw_message_set(pbw_message *, uint32_t number, pbw_value *)` takes ownership of the value on
  success only; `pbw_message_get`, `pbw_message_clear`, `pbw_message_set_message`.
- `pbw_value_new_{int,uint,bool,float,double,string,bytes,message}`, typed getters
  (`pbw_value_get_int32`, `pbw_value_get_string`, ...), repeated access with `pbw_value_count` /
  `pbw_value_at`.
- `pbw_status pbw_encode(const pbw_message *, uint8_t **out, size_t *len)` ->
  `pbw_free()`; `pbw_status pbw_decode(const pbw_descriptor *, const void *buf, size_t len,
  pbw_message **out)` -> `pbw_message_free()`.
- `pbw_ctx *pbw_ctx_new(void)`: one arena + encode buffer per thread; `pbw_decode_ctx`,
  `pbw_encode_ctx`, `pbw_ctx_reset` (frees the whole tree at once), `pbw_ctx_used`, `pbw_ctx_free`.

## Key facts

- Explicit presence: a field absent on the wire stays absent; no defaults are filled in.
- Wire data is untrusted input: lengths bounds-checked, field number 0 and wire types above 5
  rejected, nesting capped at 100 (`PBW_MAX_DEPTH`), every failure returns a `pbw_status`.
- Descriptors are trusted input; loading adversarial descriptor sets is out of scope.
- Dynamic schema loading: `pbw_descriptor_set_load()` reads a standard `FileDescriptorSet` produced by
  `protoc --include_imports --descriptor_set_out`, `buf build -o`, or the optional `pbwire-protoc`
  library. Every imported file must be in the set (types resolve by name), otherwise the load fails
  with `unknown type ... for field ...` in `pbw_schema_error()`. The loader reads names, numbers,
  types, labels, oneofs, `packed` and the file syntax; services, extensions and source info are
  ignored. proto3/edition-2023 sets get packed repetition by default.
- The schema owns its descriptors and must outlive every message, value and `pbw_ctx` tree built from
  it; treat a linked schema as read-only while other threads use it.
- Unknown fields (including a known field with the wrong wire type) are preserved as raw wire bytes
  and re-emitted after the known fields, in input order.
- No globals and no thread-local state: confine a schema or message to one thread. One `pbw_ctx` per
  thread gives arena reuse; messages decoded through a context are read-only and freed by
  `pbw_ctx_reset`.
- Numbers are raw bit patterns; the descriptor type decides which typed getter applies. Repeated
  numeric fields accept both packed and unpacked encodings; the descriptor controls encoding, and
  proto3 schemas loaded from a `FileDescriptorSet` get packed defaults.
- Two independent libraries in one repository: `pbwire` (pure C, no dependency) and
  `pbwire-protoc` (C++17 + libprotobuf, `.proto` -> `FileDescriptorSet`). They meet only at the
  serialized descriptor set.
- Not implemented: JSON/text format mapping, RPC/HTTP, groups as fields (skipped on decode),
  extension resolution, `required` enforcement, code generation.

## Optional

- [tests/test_pbwire.c](tests/test_pbwire.c): golden `protoc 36.2` bytes and edge cases, usable as
  executable examples.
- [bench/bench.cc](bench/bench.cc): differential test and benchmark against libprotobuf C++
  (generated code and `DynamicMessage`).
- [conformance/testee.c](conformance/testee.c): testee for Google's `conformance_test_runner`, binary
  wire format only.
